# @satorufx/mediadownloader

Download video, audio and images from any supported platform with one function call. No API key, no cookies, no ffmpeg.

Powered by [api.satoru.click](https://api.satoru.click).

```bash
npm install @satorufx/mediadownloader
```

## Quick start

```js
const { download } = require('@satorufx/mediadownloader');

const result = await download('https://www.tiktok.com/@tiktok/video/7106594312292453675');

console.log(result.title);   // "how many frogs did you find? ..."
console.log(result.video);   // direct mp4 link, no watermark
console.log(result.audio);   // background audio link
```

ESM works too:

```js
import { download } from '@satorufx/mediadownloader';
```

## Save to disk

```js
const { save } = require('@satorufx/mediadownloader');

await save('https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ', 'video.mp4');
await save('https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ', './downloads/', { type: 'audio' });
```

Pass a path ending in a slash and the filename comes from the title.

## Command line

```bash
npx @satorufx/mediadownloader "https://www.tiktok.com/@user/video/123"
npx @satorufx/mediadownloader "https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ" -q 720p -o video.mp4
npx @satorufx/mediadownloader "https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ" -t audio -o ./downloads/
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `-o, --out <path>` | Save to disk; a trailing slash means "directory" |
| `-t, --type <kind>` | `video` or `audio`. Default `video` |
| `-q, --quality <q>` | `best` `worst` `360p` `720p` `1080p` … |
| `-e, --endpoint <name>` | Use a specific API endpoint |
| `--resolve` | Resolve progress-stream links up front |
| `--json` | Print raw JSON |
| `--endpoints` | List available endpoints |

## Supported platforms

Any `http(s)` URL is accepted. Every request goes through one endpoint that handles all platforms — YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, Threads, Pinterest, Spotify, SoundCloud, Douyin, Bilibili, CapCut, Xiaohongshu, Shopee, Zing MP3, XVideos and more.

There is no per-platform routing to configure and nothing to keep in sync as the API grows.

## Result shape

Every response is normalized into the same object, so nothing downstream has to care which platform the URL came from:

```js
{
  ok: true,
  platform: 'tiktok',
  sourceUrl: 'https://...',
  endpoint: 'downallv2',
  title: 'how many frogs...',
  author: 'TikTok',
  thumbnail: 'https://...',
  duration: 24,             // always seconds
  durationRaw: 24564,       // untouched API value
  media: [                  // every link found, best first
    { type: 'video', url: 'https://...', quality: 'hd_no_watermark', pending: false },
    { type: 'video', url: 'https://...', quality: 'no_watermark',    pending: false },
    { type: 'audio', url: 'https://...', quality: null,              pending: false }
  ],
  video: 'https://...',     // pick for the requested quality
  audio: 'https://...',
  videoQuality: 'hd_no_watermark',
  pending: false,           // true if any link still needs resolving
  images: [],               // for slideshow posts
  raw: { ... }              // original payload
}
```

Need a field this package does not map? It is in `raw`.

## Choosing quality

```js
await download(url, { quality: 'best' });   // highest available
await download(url, { quality: '720p' });   // exact match, or closest tier
await download(url, { quality: 'worst' });  // smallest file
```

Quality labels differ by platform — YouTube reports `144p` through `2160p`, TikTok reports `hd_no_watermark` / `no_watermark` / `watermark`, Facebook reports `HD` / `SD`. All of them are ranked on one scale, so `'best'` and `'720p'` behave sensibly everywhere.

With no preference, the best option up to 1080p is chosen. Higher tiers are much larger files for little practical gain.

## Progress-stream links

Some YouTube links are not files. They are streams that report server-side encoding progress and only reveal the real file URL in their final event. Those arrive with `pending: true`.

`save()`, `videoUrl()` and `audioUrl()` handle this for you. For `download()`, opt in:

```js
const result = await download(url, {
  resolve: true,
  onProgress: ({ percent, status }) => console.log(`${status} ${percent}%`)
});

result.video   // direct file link
result.pending // false
```

Resolving waits for the server to finish encoding, which takes around 25 seconds for a typical video. Skip `resolve` when you only need metadata.

You can also resolve a link yourself later:

```js
const { resolveUrl, needsResolve } = require('@satorufx/mediadownloader');

if (needsResolve(link)) {
  const { url } = await resolveUrl(link);
}
```

## Client options

```js
const { MediaDownloader } = require('@satorufx/mediadownloader');

const client = new MediaDownloader({
  timeout: 90000,   // ms, default 60000
  retries: 3,       // default 2
  baseUrl: 'https://api.satoru.click'
});

const result = await client.download(url);
console.log(client.lastRateLimit);  // { limit: 100, remaining: 99, reset: '...' }
```

Shortcuts that return a ready-to-use link:

```js
const videoLink = await client.videoUrl(url);
const audioLink = await client.audioUrl(url);
```

## Targeting a specific endpoint

The default endpoint covers every platform. To call a different one:

```js
await download(url, { endpoint: 'youtubedl' });
await client.fromEndpoint('downallv4', url, { quality: '360p' });
```

`MediaDownloader.endpoints` lists them all.

## Error handling

```js
const { download, MediaDownloaderError } = require('@satorufx/mediadownloader');

try {
  await download(url);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof MediaDownloaderError) {
    console.error(error.code, error.status);
  }
}
```

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_URL` | Not an http/https URL |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Over the request limit |
| `NO_MEDIA` | API responded but had no links |
| `TIMEOUT` | Request took too long |
| `RESOLVE_FAILED` | A progress stream ended without a file URL |
| `UPSTREAM` | Error from the API |

Transient failures (429, 502, 503, 504, 521) are retried automatically with backoff.

## Rate limits

The API allows 100 requests per window. Remaining quota is on `client.lastRateLimit` and in the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header.

## TypeScript

Type declarations ship with the package — no `@types` install needed.

```ts
import { download, DownloadResult } from '@satorufx/mediadownloader';

const result: DownloadResult = await download(url);
```

## Requirements

Node.js 18 or newer, for built-in `fetch`. Zero dependencies.
